explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM evaluators against human judgments using Pearson correlation analysis and reports quantitative scores for agreement across multiple evaluation dimensions and models

prompts.notes: Full prompts provided in appendix tables for key-fact validation (Table 21), multi-agent debate (Advocate - Table 24, Adjudicator - Table 26), and key-fact alignment assessment

guidelines.notes: Human evaluation uses two main tasks: fact verification using error taxonomy (out-of-article, entity, relation, sentence errors) and key-fact alignment similar to NLI task. Guidelines detailed in Section 4.2 and Appendix C

sample_size.notes: Total of 1,200 English summaries (25 docs × 6 domains × 8 models) and 1,050 Chinese summaries (25 docs × 6 domains × 7 models). All evaluated by both LLM and human.

quantitative_scores.notes: Qwen-2.5-72B stands out for strong performance in faithfulness evaluation
Significant variability in LLM evaluation accuracy across dimensions
Performance varies across domains and languages

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM evaluation accuracy varies significantly across evaluation dimensions, domains, and languages. Strong correlation (ρ=0.71) found between LLM performance in summarization and evaluation tasks, but no single model consistently achieves best performance across all dimensions.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same three primary dimensions (faithfulness, completeness, conciseness) and two stability metrics. Human evaluation incorporates multi-agent debate assistance while LLM evaluation includes additional self-evaluation bias analysis.
